summary: The article provides a generally accurate and comprehensive overview of the RBI's FCNR(B) swap window and FCNR(B) deposits, with most factual claims aligning with authoritative sources.

claims.claim: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has reintroduced a special FCNR(B) swap window for banks to attract Non-Resident Indian (NRI) deposits.
claims.note: The RBI announced the reintroduction of the FCNR(B) swap facility on June 5, 2026, with operational guidelines issued on June 8, 2026.

claims.claim: This scheme, known as the FCNR(B) swap window, was last used in 2013 when the rupee was facing significant pressure.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm the FCNR(B) swap window was last used in 2013.

claims.claim: This intervention successfully attracted over USD 34 billion in inflows, helping to stabilise the rupee and shore up India's foreign exchange reserves.
claims.note: The 2013 scheme collectively brought in $34 billion, with the FCNR(B) swap against deposits raising $26 billion.

claims.claim: FCNR(B) accounts are term deposit accounts denominated in foreign currencies, such as US Dollars (USD), British Pounds (GBP), Euros (EUR), Japanese Yen (JPY), and Canadian Dollars (CAD), held by Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) and Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs) in India.
claims.note: FCNR(B) accounts are indeed term deposits for NRIs/PIOs in India, and the listed currencies (USD, GBP, EUR, JPY, CAD) are among the designated currencies. Australian Dollars (AUD) are also commonly included.

claims.claim: Interest earned on FCNR(B) deposits is exempt from income tax in India for NRIs.
claims.note: Interest earned on FCNR(B) deposits is exempt from income tax in India for NRIs.

claims.claim: The scheme will remain open for deposits mobilised until 30 September 2026, while banks can access the swap facility until 16 October 2026.
claims.note: The swap facility is available for deposits mobilized between June 8 and September 30, 2026, and the swap window will remain open until October 16, 2026.

claims.claim: The 2013 window was for FCNR deposits maturing in three years, while the one announced now covers deposits maturing in three to five years.
claims.note: The 2013 scheme was for FCNR(B) deposits with a minimum three-year maturity, while the current scheme covers maturities of three to five years.

article_title: RBI Revives FCNR(B) Swap Window: Can It Attract NRI Inflows?
